## Theory path — Understand

We first observe what an LLM predicts, then reconstruct the computation that produces its predictive distribution. We next examine context design before distinguishing three uses of that same distribution: generating a continuation, scoring an observed sequence, and learning the parameters. The nine stages below give the first-reading order; the resource map further down supports exploration beyond that order without adding prerequisites.

### Learning path skeleton {#conceptual-route}

The details of each lesson follow the form **ideas used → object studied · intended outcome**.

{{< include ../includes/generated-conceptual-route-en.qmd >}}

<details>
<summary>Predictions in notation</summary>

For an autoregressive GPT, $f_\theta(c)$ maps context $c$ to logits using parameters $\theta$. Normalizing the logits gives the base next-token distribution.

$$p_\theta(\cdot\mid c)=\operatorname{softmax}\!\bigl(f_\theta(c)\bigr).$$

</details>

### The nine stages {#guided-stages}

These stages follow the canonical curriculum. They show the study order and optional resources. Pages within a stage complement one another.

**Other primary path — Build:** To build a small GPT, follow the [independent Build path](build-path.html). It has its own implementation milestones and prerequisites; it is not a required continuation of the Theory path. Corpus preparation and training-example construction form a dedicated model-learning branch, not a prerequisite for inference.

## Explore the resources

<details>
<summary>How to read this map</summary>

- **Territories** — the main parts of the site: Understand, Build, Practice, Deepen, Reference.
- **Sections** — clicking a territory reveals its subsections; the breadcrumb or the Escape key takes you back up one level at a time.
- **Pages** — clicking a page shows its details (purpose, sections, links); "Open the page" navigates there directly.
- **Concepts** — the "Canonical concepts" view groups the concepts from the bilingual registry versioned in `data/concepts.yml` by discovery domain, with their definitions, typed relationships, and resource pages. The search and the relation-type filter narrow the list, a selected concept highlights its neighbours, and related concepts remain clickable from the details panel.

Section headings shown in a page's details are editorial landmarks, not canonical concepts. The guided route provides a reading order.

The URL records the search, filter, and selection. “Copy link” shares that view. “Reset view” clears those three settings. The map and static list are generated from the Quarto sidebar and page metadata.

</details>

{{< include ../includes/generated-map-territories-en.qmd >}}

{{< include ../includes/generated-map-data-en.qmd >}}

Use this map for orientation, not as a strict prerequisite graph. Advanced pages can be consulted directly when they address the question at hand.
